# Credits and data licenses

This is a non-commercial hackathon project. BatNet is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and most
of our iNaturalist photos are CC BY-NC. Each source keeps its own license;
this page records credits rather than assigning a new license to third-party work.

## BatNet

Krivek G. et al. (2023). "BatNet: a deep learning-based tool for automated bat
species identification from camera trap images". *Remote Sensing in Ecology and
Conservation*. [Paper / DOI](https://doi.org/10.1002/rse2.339).

[BatNet code and model](https://github.com/GabiK-bat/BatNet), by Gabriella Krivek
and collaborators, supply the pretrained detector and species classifier.
License: [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/),
as stated in the [BatNet repository](https://github.com/GabiK-bat/BatNet).
Our project fine-tunes the detector; the species classifier remains unchanged.

## iNaturalist photos

Thanks to the photographers and observers who share their work through
[iNaturalist](https://www.inaturalist.org/). The counts and full attribution list
below were generated with inline Python from
[data/inaturalist/photos.csv](data/inaturalist/photos.csv), using its `image`,
`license`, `attribution`, and `observation` fields. Metadata snapshot: 2026-10-03.
These counts cover downloaded photos before label acceptance, held-back splits,
and quality exclusions; they are not training or evaluation results.

| License recorded in metadata | Photos |
| --- | ---: |
| CC BY-NC (`cc-by-nc`) | 6,829 |
| CC BY (`cc-by`) | 1,026 |
| CC0 (`cc0`) | 81 |
| **Total** | **7,936** |

The attribution text and license code for each photo are preserved below.
Observation links point to the original context and photographer information.
The downloader resizes photos and saves JPEG copies; training may crop or augment
these images. The metadata does not give a license version for every photo, so
none is assumed here.

## Google Open Images Dataset (V6/V7)

Thanks to Google, the Open Images annotators, and the individual image authors.
[Dataset website](https://storage.googleapis.com/openimages/web/index.html).
The download tools use V6 training box annotations, V5 validation/test box
annotations, and V7 class names.

The local [annotations.csv](data/openimages/annotations.csv) lists **2,674
unique images** across training and validation, in **2,855 rows**
(some photos have multiple bat boxes), before quality exclusions.

Annotations are licensed by Google LLC under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Images are listed as
[CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/) by their respective
authors. These are the dataset's stated licenses; local box annotations do not
include individual author or image-license metadata. See the official
[Open Images license information](https://storage.googleapis.com/openimages/web/factsfigures.html#licenses)
and [image metadata](https://storage.googleapis.com/openimages/web/download_v7.html#image-info)
for those source records.

## Synthetic and local images

`training/synthesize_data.py` creates composites from training bat crops and
Open Images or local room backgrounds. Synthetic images are modified examples,
not additional wildlife observations; source-image license terms still apply.
`training/capture_room_negatives.py` supplies local webcam backgrounds with no
bats in view. Synthetic labels and a preview are in `data/synthetic/`.

## Software

- **PyTorch** and its contributors: model execution, GPU support, and training.
  [Project](https://pytorch.org/) and [BSD-style license](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/LICENSE).
- **torchvision** and its contributors: image transforms and detection operations.
  [Project](https://github.com/pytorch/vision) and [BSD 3-Clause license](https://github.com/pytorch/vision/blob/main/LICENSE).
- **OpenCV** and its contributors: webcam capture, motion detection, image
  processing, display, and snapshots, through `opencv-python`.
  [Project and Apache 2.0 license information](https://opencv.org/about/).
